TasteMaster Foods - Q2 2024 Earnings Call Transcript

**Operator:**
Good morning, and welcome to the TasteMaster Foods Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. Today's conference is being recorded. At this time, I would like to inform you that this call is being webcast live and simultaneously archived for replay. A replay will be available on the company's website shortly after the call concludes.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

**Sarah Johnson (Head of Investor Relations):**
Thank you, operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss TasteMaster Foods' Q2 2024 results. Joining me on the call are Alex Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Elena Vasquez, Chief Financial Officer; Raj Patel, Chief Growth Officer; and Maria Gonzalez, Chief Supply Chain Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call may contain forward-looking statements within the meaning of the safe harbor provisions of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995. Please refer to our SEC filings, including our most recent Form 10-K and 10-Q, for a discussion of the factors that could cause actual results to differ materially from these statements.

With that, I'll turn the call over to Alex.

**Alex Thompson (CEO):**
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. We are pleased to report our results for Q2 2024. We delivered strong performance despite ongoing macroeconomic headwinds and inflationary pressures.

Today, I'll be focusing on five key areas: overall company performance highlights, organic revenue growth overall and by region, market share trends for major brands, capital expenditure plans and priorities, and EPS guidance and key assumptions.

First, regarding overall company performance highlights. We're thrilled with how our portfolio demonstrated resilience and strategic execution this quarter. For the period ended June 30, 2024, we posted net revenues of $15.8 billion, up 9% year-over-year on a reported basis and 7% organically, surpassing our guidance midpoint thanks to strength in both volume and pricing. Organic growth reflected a solid blend of 3% volume increases and 4% net pricing realization. Volumes were widespread, especially in healthier categories where we picked up 120 basis points of market share according to IRI and Nielsen data. Our pricing strategy has proven resilient to consumers, with no significant drop in elasticity—household penetration for brands like Zest Cola Zero Sugar and CrunchMax bars stayed firm at 85% in North America.

Profitability outperformed too. Adjusted gross margin widened 210 basis points to 41.8%, powered by supply chain gains like a 15% drop in logistics expenses through our enhanced distribution center network, which is now 95% automated using AI route optimization in collaboration with partners like Maersk. This cushioned a 200 basis point foreign exchange drag from the stronger dollar. Adjusted operating margin reached 18.2%, up 160 basis points, yielding adjusted EBITDA of $3.1 billion at a 19.6% margin and 12% growth year-over-year. Free cash flow hit an impressive $2.2 billion, enabling $1.5 billion returned to shareholders via repurchases and dividends, while keeping net debt-to-EBITDA at a healthy 2.1 times.

By segment, beverages, which make up 55% of revenues, advanced 10% organically to $8.7 billion, with 5% volume gains in sparkling lines amid premiumization—our VitaSurge Energy is now the number two in convenience stores behind Red Bull, with average unit volumes up 18%. Hydration plays like PureSpring alkaline water grabbed two share points against rivals like Dasani. Snacks and confectionery, 30% of the mix, grew 6% organically to $4.7 billion, led by ZestChips salty snacks with 4% volume on innovations like plant-based sriracha-lime flavors; chocolate categories faced cocoa inflation headwinds, but we hedged 80% of fiscal 2024 needs at $4,200 per ton. Convenience foods, our high-growth 15% slice, jumped 12% to $2.4 billion, riding the $50 billion foodservice-at-home trend with ready-to-eat meals.

Geographically, it was balanced. North America, 60% of revenues, surged 11% organically to $9.5 billion—our best quarter in years—thanks to club stores like Costco where reloads rose 25%, and e-commerce now 18% of the region's sales, beating Amazon's category pace. We took 1.5 share points per Circana, pulling from private labels. EMEA, 20%, grew 4% organically to $3.2 billion despite 5% volume softness from UK living costs and German sugar taxes; our zero-sugar shift to 45% of the portfolio from 30% last year minimized the hit. APAC and Latin America together, 20%, accelerated 12% to $3.1 billion, with India hydration packs up 15% in volume and Brazil premium beer tie-ups adding 300 basis points; China's high-sugar scrutiny slowed us to flat, but yogurt ramps are underway.

These outcomes affirm our Health Forward, Portfolio Power strategy. We've rolled out 25 new SKUs this half, 70% better-for-you like plant-based and low-sugar options, tapping the $250 billion wellness shift per Euromonitor. Our $500 million GenAI supply chain platform from Q1 cut forecast errors to 2% from 8%, aiding just-in-time sourcing for volatile cocoa. Sustainability advanced with 25% year-to-date Scope 3 cuts via regenerative farming with 50,000 partners, hitting top-quartile MSCI ESG ratings and complying with EU deforestation rules. Following last year's $1.2 billion Kind Snacks add-on, we're scouting functional beverage tuck-ins for 10%+ long-term organic growth.

Second, concerning organic revenue growth overall and by region. Our organic revenue rose 4.2% for the quarter, beating guidance and marking six straight quarters of gains, with year-to-date at 4.8% toward our full-year 4% to 5% goal. This strips out 1.2% from the PureBites organic snack acquisition and 150 basis points from dollar strength in emerging markets. It stemmed from 1.8% pricing and 2.4% volume/mix, balancing value capture with loyalty via innovation and promos.

Regionally, North America at 55% of revenues led with 5.8% growth. Beverages shone via VitaQuench functional hydration up 12% in volume on premium electrolyte SKUs, echoing Gatorade trends, plus 2.5% pricing on carbonated lines without pushback. Snacks added 4.2%, grabbing 110 basis points share in clean-label nuts and plant-based bars under TasteMaster Clean—40% of the portfolio now free of artificial preservatives ahead of California regs. E-commerce hit 18% of sales from 12%, with DTC app repeats up 25%.

EMEA, 25% of revenues, delivered 3.1%, curbed by Western Europe energy costs and HFSS regs. Beverages grew 2.9% on zero-calorie sparklers in UK/Germany with recyclable aluminum cans partnering Ball Corporation for EU plastics compliance. Snacks led at 4.5% with EuroCrunch kettle chips in truffle-seaweed flavors. Volume/mix edged up 0.8%, pricing 2.3% against wheat/oil inflation peaks.

APAC, 15%, topped at 6.5% from urbanization. ReadyMeal pouches in Thai/Indian flavors drove 8.2% convenience volumes; China's almond milks rose 15% like Oatly, via Shanghai pea protein R&D. Pricing added 1.7%, with kirana expansions in Indonesia/Vietnam via Gojek.

Latin America, 5%, eased to 2.9% amid Brazil/Argentina inflation. BevEssentials hydration packs held volumes at 1.5%, pricing 3.4% offset by value packs and Rewards app covering 70% footprint. A Bimbo JV for tortilla chips cut freight 15%.

Forward levers include premiumization with 25 SKUs, 60% health-focused like keto snacks and adaptogen drinks; DTC to 25% of revenues by 2025 via AI personalization; and blockchain traceability cutting Scope 3 12% while lifting NPS 300 basis points. We're lifting full-year organic to 4.5-5.5%, Q3 at the top end.

Third, in terms of market share trends for major brands. In a 2.8% growing global F&B market squeezed by inflation, supply issues, and health shifts, we gained 110 basis points to 24.5% combined share in beverages/snacks per Nielsen/IRI, our best since early 2020.

Flagship Zest Cola holds 32.1% U.S. dollar share in CSDs, up 1.8 points quarterly and 90 bps YoY through multi-outlet/e-com. This beat Coke's 40 bps drop to 41.2% and Pepsi's flat 18.7%, via flat pricing amid 7-9% COGS hikes versus rivals' 4-6%. Velocity rose 3.2% on Zest Zero Heroes, 15% of zero-sugar CSDs up 12% volume, with stevia-erythritol reformulation winning 85% blind tests over Coke Zero.

VitaSurge energy drinks hit 22.4% North America share, up 2.1 points YoY over Monster's 1.2-point loss to 19.8% and flat Red Bull 28.5%, via 25% trade spend on coolers/displays lifting ACV to 92%. In APAC, China share jumped 4.5 points to 14.2% on Tmall/JD e-com for nootropic taurine-caffeine-L-theanine blends, convenience velocity up 11%.

CrunchMax salty snacks steady at 27.3% U.S., +60 bps over Lay's 0.8-point dip to 34.1%, via air-fried 40% less oil crisps up 22% volume, 8% BFY subsegment post-Ozempic. Global up 1.4 to 19.8%, EMEA strong amid Mondelez Oreo tax pressures.

North America portfolio at 29.7%, +1.5 points on at-home rebound and QSR like McDonald's Zest pours. EMEA +80 bps to 21.2%, recyclable PET edging Coke. APAC +2.3 to 18.9%, India VitaSurge +5.2 festive; LATAM +0.9 to 16.4%, Mexico near-beer.

Drivers: $450M R&D for natural sweeteners, zero-sugar on 70% SKUs; omnichannel e-com 14% sales, Amazon 95% ACV, DTC bundles 20% repeats; regenerative soy on 50,000 acres up brand equity 12 points YouGov. Expect 100-150 bps FY24 gains to 26%, hedged 80% commodities.

Fourth, looking at capital expenditure plans and priorities. We're in a key phase, investing disciplinedly to sustain mid-single-digit organic growth against inflation and consumer shifts. FY2024 capex stays $650 million, 4.2% of sales, up 12% from $580 million last year, on higher-ROI for throughput, resilience, sustainability. Q2 deployed $320 million, 49% YTD, free cash conversion 95-100%, net debt/EBITDA 2.1x.

Priority 1: Manufacturing capacity/automation, 40% or $260M. Modernizing 45 plants for 8-10% capacity boost vs. 5% CAGR demand in plant-based snacks/RTD. Key: $120M brownfield NA expansions, $45M Chicago VitaCrunch line with Tetra Pak like Nestlé's, +25% output for $15B healthy snacking. $90M automation ABB/Rockwell; Europe $30M Dutch like Unilever Hellmann's, -15% labor, OEE +3 to 88%. NA 55%, APAC 30% Indonesia.

Priority 2: Supply chain resilience/distribution, 30% $195M. For 20% lead time cuts, 10% logistics savings FY25. $100M three DCs, Dallas 500k sq ft AutoStore like Mondelez Oreos. $60M cold chain reefer IoT for FreshBite; LATAM $35M Brazil vs. El Niño like Coke. APAC 40% Mumbai for India 15% imports; Europe nearshoring EUDR.

Priority 3: Sustainability/ESG, 20% $130M. Toward 2030 net-zero, 25% Scope 1/2 cuts. $70M solar/biogas, California $25M 30% onsite like Danone. $40M water Veolia, 20% intensity down, Australia pilot 18% like Nestlé CSV. Europe 50% CSRD/PFAS; NA regenerative organics.

Priority 4: Digital/innovation, 10% $65M. AI to 92% forecast accuracy vs. sugar taxes. $30M SAP/Blue Yonder like P&G; $20M Singapore fermentation for $8B APAC alt-proteins.

NPV vetted >15% IRR, <4yr payback; $120M savings FY26 for 2-3 margin points. Mitigate steel tariffs fixed contracts, pause $50M for M&A functional bevs. Positions us ahead of Kraft Heinz efficiency, 8-10% EPS CAGR.

Finally, reviewing EPS guidance and key assumptions. On adjusted basis, excluding $45M LATAM restructuring and $28M Europe dairy divest gain, FY2024 EPS guides $5.85-$6.10, 9-14% growth midpoint over $5.35 prior. Assumes 24.5% tax, 428M shares on $1.2B buybacks, $0.05 FX headwind USD/euro/BRL.

Top-line: 5-7% organic, 2-3% volume/mix from Zest Sparkling, Harvest NutriBars, PureLeaf—65% 2023 growth drivers. Plant-based OatFlex/VeggieCrunch +15%, e-com 18% NA. NA 55% mid-single via QSR McD/Starbucks Zest Zero. Europe 25% flat-1% CC, 4% pricing/5% healthier vols like Unilever. APAC/LATAM 20% 8-10%, India RTD teas/Brazil snacks 12%.

Gross margin +150 bps to 38.5% on $250M savings: $120M procurement 70% cocoa $3,200/ton hedged vs. 25% surge; $80M mfg AI Texas waste -12%; nearshoring Mexico. Op margin +100 bps 14.2%, SG&A 50 bps ZBB/digital TikTok 4.5x ROI. $450M capex 4.5% sales on sugarcane/packaging.

Health Forward: 60% innovation functional like protein Zest+, low-sodium snacks 11% CAGR. M&A $300M IndieJuice; $800M FCF for buybacks 2-3% yield, 3.1% dividend +8%, debt 2.2x.

Risks: CPI 2.5%, commodities hedged 80% sugar+5/dairy flat/corn+3; no recession but 1% GDP shave -$0.15 EPS; Red Sea +10% freight.

Overall, we are confident in our ability to navigate the current environment and deliver long-term value for our shareholders.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Elena to provide more detail on our financial results.

**Elena Vasquez (CFO):**
Thank you, Alex. As Alex mentioned, we achieved solid results in Q2 2024. Net sales were $15.8 billion, representing a 9% increase year-over-year. Gross margin was 41.8%, impacted by supply chain efficiencies that more than offset input cost inflation. Operating income was $2.9 billion, and earnings per share were $1.55. We are managing our costs effectively and continue to invest in key growth initiatives.

Our balance sheet remains strong with $4.5 billion in cash and marketable securities. We are committed to returning value to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases.

For the full year, we are reaffirming our guidance for adjusted EPS of $5.85 to $6.10.

Now, let's open the call for questions.

**Operator:**
Ladies and gentlemen, at this time we will begin the question-and-answer session. [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from Mike Carter with Deutsche Bank. Please proceed.

**Mike Carter (Deutsche Bank):**
Good morning. Can you provide more color on the impact of inflation on your business?

**Alex Thompson (CEO):**
Good morning, Mike. Inflation remains a challenge, particularly in commodities like cocoa up 25%, coffee, dairy 40% YTD, and logistics from Red Sea issues adding 10%. We've navigated it through disciplined pricing up 1.8-4% selectively, holding elasticity steady, while hedging 70-80% of needs—cocoa at $3,200-$4,200/ton, corn +3%, aluminum +10%. Supply chain savings of $250M run-rate, including 15% logistics cuts and manufacturing efficiencies like AI forecasting reducing waste 12%, expanded gross margins 150-210 bps. This protects our 38.5-41.8% targets while investing in premium health formats where consumers trade up.

**Operator:**
Our next question comes from Sarah Lee with Morgan Stanley. Please proceed.

**Sarah Lee (Morgan Stanley):**
Thanks. What are your plans for new plant-based beverages and what is the expected revenue impact?

**Raj Patel (Chief Growth Officer):**
Thanks, Sarah. Our plant-based beverages, like expanded OatFlex milks and VeggieCrunch extensions, are central to Health Forward. We're investing $450M R&D including precision fermentation for natural alt-proteins, rolling zero-sugar to 70% SKUs. Q2 volumes +15% organically, e-com 18%, targeting $8B APAC space with Singapore lab. Expect 1-2 points FY24 revenue lift, 10-12% category growth via omnichannel—DTC app +25% repeats, Amazon 95% ACV—and sustainability like regenerative ag boosting equity 12 points. Full ramp mid-double digits long-term.

**Operator:**
Our next question comes from Tom Rivera with Barclays. Please proceed.

**Tom Rivera (Barclays):**
How are you managing supply chain disruptions?

**Maria Gonzalez (Chief Supply Chain Officer):**
Good question, Tom. Post-pandemic and Red Sea delays, we're fortifying with $195M capex on resilience: three new automated DCs like Dallas AutoStore cutting fulfillment 40%, cold chain IoT/reefer electrification for perishables like FreshBite, LATAM $35M vs. crop volatility. Nearshoring 30% Mexico imports, diversified soy-canola vs. palm shortages. GenAI platform slashed errors 2%, OEE +3 to 88%, lead times -20% target. Hedging 80% FX/commodities, fixed contracts vs. tariffs. Positions us for 10% logistics savings FY25.

**Operator:**
Our last question comes from Lisa Kim with Citi. Please proceed.

**Lisa Kim (Citi):**
What is your outlook for the rest of the year?

**Elena Vasquez (CFO):**
Thanks, Lisa. Q3 organic 6-8%, full-year 4.5-5.5%, EPS $5.85-6.10 midpoint 11-12% growth. Assumes moderating CPI 2.5%, hedged inputs, no recession—volume from power brands/health premiumization, margin +150 bps on $250M savings, capex $650M high-ROI. Upside from 100-150 bps share gains, e-com/DTC acceleration, M&A bolt-ons. Risks like GDP shave -$0.15 covered by agility vs. peers.

**Operator:**
I would now like to turn the call back over to Alex for closing remarks.

**Alex Thompson (CEO):**
Thank you for your questions and your continued interest in TasteMaster Foods. We are focused on executing our strategy and delivering strong results. We look forward to updating you on our progress next quarter.

**Operator:**
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
